recommendedExperiment: Synthesize or select Al-MOF host with reproducible phase purity.
expectedObservation: Al-MOF host shows stable pre-reaction PXRD and accessible pore signature.
successCriterion: Host phase and baseline pore-access proxy are reproducible before Mo introduction.

purpose: Introduce Mo as guest / dopant / electronic modulation site.
recommendedExperiment: Introduce Mo by doping / post-synthetic modification / bimetallic node construction in parallel micro-batches.
expectedObservation: Mo is incorporated or anchored without destroying the Al-MOF scaffold.
successCriterion: A Mo-containing Al-MOF route retains structure and shows measurable Mo incorporation.

recommendedExperiment: Compare pristine Al-MOF and Al-MOF + Mo before reaction by PXRD, FTIR, ICP, and microscopy.
expectedObservation: The host scaffold remains identifiable and Mo distribution is not a separate bulk oxide-only phase.
successCriterion: Pre-reaction evidence supports a host-guest or doped route rather than simple physical contamination.

recommendedExperiment: Run 170C aqueous stability hold before catalytic testing.
expectedObservation: Al-MOF + Mo retains framework signature and shows limited metal leaching.
successCriterion: Framework retention and leaching remain within predefined validation limits.

purpose: Compare formic acid production with pristine Al-MOF.
recommendedExperiment: Run paired formic-acid reaction tests for Al-MOF + Mo, pristine Al-MOF, MoOx alone, physical mixture, and blank.
expectedObservation: Al-MOF + Mo improves formic-acid / formate signal relative to pristine Al-MOF without uncontrolled side-product growth.
riskAddressed: high-priority hypothesis not final catalytic proof
successCriterion: Improvement over pristine Al-MOF is statistically visible in early validation data.

purpose: Characterize Mo coordination state before and after reaction.
recommendedExperiment: Track Mo coordination and oxidation-state proxies before and after aqueous reaction.
expectedObservation: Mo remains associated with the host route and does not fully leach or collapse to an unrelated phase.
successCriterion: Mo speciation is traceable enough to support or falsify the guest-metal mechanism.

purpose: Evaluate whether Mo improves CO2 activation / HCOO* stabilization.
recommendedExperiment: Run isotope or intermediate-trapping experiments and compare with pristine Al-MOF controls.
expectedObservation: Mo route shows stronger C1 activation or formate-intermediate signal than host-only control.
successCriterion: Mechanistic evidence supports Mo as activity compensation rather than a passive additive.

recommendedExperiment: Run Al-MOF + Fe as a lower-priority dopant control only after Mo feasibility is resolved.
expectedObservation: Fe route clarifies whether redox dopants create side-product leakage.
successCriterion: Control route quantifies whether redox dopants are beneficial or risky.
